chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rabie ibn Abdullah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Safety of the Religion and good health of the body is better than wealth, and wealth is an adornment from the adornments of the world, an excellence.
Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad, from Rabie, from Al-Fuzayl, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) – similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the value of wealth compared to health and religion in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes a hierarchy of values where the preservation of faith and bodily health outweighs material accumulation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on holistic well-being as a prerequisite for spiritual duty. While wealth is acknowledged as a legitimate worldly adornment (zīnat al-dunyā), it is subordinate to the internal state of the soul and the physical vessel that enables worship. This narration underscores the practical wisdom that spiritual safety is the foundation upon which all other blessings rest.
